summary.tldr: Amalgamates the Ottawa and Alexandria-Cornwall Roman Catholic corporations into one new Ottawa-Cornwall corporation.
what_it_does: Creates The Roman Catholic Episcopal Corporation of Ottawa-Cornwall by merging the Ottawa corporation and the Alexandria-Cornwall corporation.
Transfers the property, debts, claims, rights, privileges, and legal proceedings of both corporations to the new corporation.
Sets the new corporation up as a not-for-profit body, with the Roman Catholic Archbishop of Ottawa-Cornwall as its sole member.
Requires the Archbishop to get written consent from one diocesan clergy member and one lay person before dealing with the corporation’s real property.

Deems the Alexandria-Cornwall corporation to have applied for, and received, continuance under the Canada Not-for-profit Corporations Act on royal assent, and repeals the 1884 federal Act for the Ottawa diocese.
who_it_affects: Roman Catholic Episcopal Corporation of Ottawa
summary.background: The bill deals with two existing corporations, one incorporated by a federal Act in 1884 and the other by Ontario legislation in 1891, later amended in 1977. It also treats the Alexandria-Cornwall corporation as having applied for continuance under the Canada Not-for-profit Corporations Act.
